memory_candidates.content: jq pitfall: inside a pipe like `X | . as $e | (EXPR) | select(([$arr[]] | index(.)) == null)`, the `.` passed to `index(.)` refers to whatever the ENCLOSING pipe stage just produced (here, the array `[$arr[]]` itself), not the value flowing from `(EXPR)` before the `select`. `index()` then searches the array inside itself and trivially returns 0 for everything, silently defeating the whole membership check. Fix: bind the value to a named variable BEFORE the select (`(EXPR) as $v | select(($arr | index($v)) == null)`), since a bound variable's value is independent of `.`'s current rebinding. Caught by a fixture test asserting an unrecognized-value case actually got flagged -- an assertion that only checks the recognized-value path would never catch this class of bug.

Shell grep pitfall when counting added/removed lines in a `git show`/`git diff` output while excluding the `+++`/`---` file-header lines: a pattern like `^\+[^+].*book_requires` looks correct but is WRONG for a genuinely added content line `+book_requires Foo`, because `[^+]` unconditionally consumes exactly one character (here the leading `b` of the content), after which `.*book_requires` must match starting from the REMAINING text (`ook_requires Foo`), which no longer contains the full literal `book_requires`. The line silently never matches. Fix: use `[^+]*` (zero-or-more, backtracking) instead of a single required non-`+` character -- `^\+[^+]*book_requires` lets the engine backtrack to zero consumed characters when needed, while still correctly excluding `+++`/`---` header lines (whose second character is itself `+`/`-`, which `[^+]*`/`[^-]*` cannot skip past). Caught only because a fixture test asserted a concrete added-line count greater than zero rather than merely asserting the field's shape/presence.

When an extension-authored schema specifies a per-group provenance marker (e.g. source: collected|backfilled) attached to several named record groups, implement the shared compute-and-emit body as ONE function parameterized by a mode flag (here is_backfill), called once by the live code path and once per item by the batch/backfill code path -- rather than writing two near-duplicate bodies. This also naturally surfaces exactly where the per-group marker needs to be threaded through, since both call sites share the same emission code.
